name: Kingdom of Galicia
alt: Kingdom of Galicia and Portugal (García II's title from 1071)

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Asturias
predecessors.text: Galicia, the share of Ordoño II when Alfonso III's lands were partitioned in 910

successors.name: Kingdom of León
successors.text: Galicia, joined to León-Castile when Alfonso VII was crowned in León on 10 March 1126

rulers.name: Ordoño II
rulers.title: king of Galicia (also king of León from 914)

rulers.name: Bermudo III
rulers.title: king of León, in refuge in Galicia

rulers.name: Alfonso VII (Alfonso Raimúndez)
rulers.title: king of Galicia under his mother Urraca

ledger.x: 910: Ordoño II becomes king of Galicia.
914: Ordoño II adds León to Galicia and the two crowns are joined.
1034: Bermudo III, driven from León by Sancho III of Pamplona, falls back on Galicia.
1035: Sancho III dies and Bermudo III is received back into León, so Galicia is again part of his Kingdom of León; it passes with León to Ferdinand I when Bermudo is killed on 4 September 1037.
1065: Ferdinand I's realm is divided and García II receives Galicia.
1065: the Taifa of Badajoz pays parias to the king of Galicia.
1071: Alfonso VI invades Galicia and García's kingdom ends.
1071: the parias of Badajoz end with the kingdom.
1111: Alfonso Raimúndez is crowned king of Galicia at Compostela.
1126: Alfonso VII is crowned in León and Galicia is joined to his kingdom.
1126: the separate kingdom of Galicia ends when Alfonso VII, king of Galicia since 1111, becomes sole ruler on 10 March 1126.

wars.name: Capture of León by Sancho III of Pamplona (1034)
wars.outcome: Sancho III took the city of León and Bermudo III retreated into Galicia; 'By the time Sancho died in 1035, the meseta north of the Duero was dominated by the Pyrenean pocket kingdom of Navarre.'

wars.name: Alfonso VI's invasion of Galicia and northern Portugal (1071)
wars.outcome: García II lost his kingdom; Sancho II defeated him in central Portugal, he fled to Seville, and in October 1072 Sancho was assassinated at Zamora, after which Alfonso 'seiz[ed] Sancho's reunited realm'.

certainty.note: Frontiers are those of an early medieval kingdom, given by rivers (the Mondego in 1065-1071) and by the pages' words; none is a treaty or survey line.

sources.title: Alfonso VII of León and Castile
